title: Walmart Earnings Beat Estimates as Revenue Rises 5.2% to $188.8 Billion, Guidance Raised
excerpt: Adjusted earnings of $0.65 a share topped expectations as U.S. online sales grew 23%, even as an investment swing cut reported profit and Flipkart's sale timing weighed on international results.
body:
• Walmart beat estimates on both lines in its fiscal third quarter: total revenue rose 5.2% to $188.8 billion and adjusted earnings rose 4.8% to $0.65 per share, ahead of the Zacks consensus of $186.5 billion and $0.64.
  • Digital drove the quarter: U.S. eCommerce sales grew 23%, global eCommerce 17%, global advertising 25% and global membership fee revenue 17%, while U.S. comparable sales rose 2.9% excluding fuel.
  • Walmart raised its fiscal 2027 outlook for the second time this year — constant-currency net sales growth of 4.9% to 5.2%, adjusted operating income growth of 8.0% to 8.6% and adjusted EPS of $2.84 to $2.89.
  • Reported EPS fell 19.5% to $0.62, because a $341 million loss on equity and other investments replaced a $2.08 billion gain a year earlier, even as operating income rose 16%.

Walmart reported fiscal third-quarter earnings on Thursday, November 19 that beat Wall Street estimates on revenue and adjusted profit, helped by fast-growing online sales, advertising and membership income heading into the holiday season. The Bentonville, Arkansas-based retailer also raised its full-year guidance for the second time in fiscal 2027.

The quarter in numbers

For the three months ended October 31, 2026, total revenue was $188.8 billion, up 5.2% from $179.5 billion a year earlier, or 4.5% in constant currency. Net sales rose 5.1% to $186.8 billion. The gross profit rate improved 28 basis points to 24.5%, and operating income rose 16.0% to $7.77 billion; adjusted operating income grew 5.5% in constant currency, faster than sales.

The gap between stronger operating profit and lower net income came from below the operating line. Net income attributable to Walmart fell 19.5% to $4.95 billion, and reported diluted EPS fell to $0.62 from $0.77, after a $341 million loss on equity and other investments, compared with a $2.08 billion gain a year earlier. Adjusted EPS, which strips out that swing, rose to $0.65 from $0.62, beating the $0.64 consensus compiled by Zacks.

U.S. stores, delivery and Sam's Club

Walmart U.S. net sales rose 3.6% to about $125.0 billion, with comparable sales excluding fuel up 2.9% — a 1.5% rise in transactions and a 1.4% rise in average ticket. Online sales rose 23%, store-fulfilled delivery grew more than 40% and marketplace sales grew about 49%, the third straight quarter above 45%. Walmart Connect advertising grew 36% excluding VIZIO and Vibe. A headwind of about 70 basis points in health and wellness, from deflation linked to Maximum Fair Price Regulation, partly offset the gains.

Sam's Club U.S. net sales rose 10% to $25.9 billion, comparable sales excluding fuel rose 4.9% on higher transactions, and eCommerce sales rose 30%. Membership fee revenue grew 2.2%. Sam's Club operating income fell 15.8% to $547 million, reflecting the absence of prior-year breakage income and an inflation-related LIFO charge.

International: China strength, Flipkart timing

Walmart International net sales rose 7% to $35.9 billion, or 3.3% in constant currency, with currency adding about $1.2 billion. China was the standout, with net sales up 28% in constant currency and eCommerce up 31%. That was partly offset in India, where the timing of Flipkart's Big Billion Days sale shifted into the fourth quarter: international eCommerce sales fell 2%, advertising fell 15%, and the shift cut about 500 basis points from constant-currency sales growth, with a corresponding benefit expected in the fourth quarter. International membership fee revenue rose 29%, and adjusted operating income rose 7% in constant currency, helped by growth in India and China.

Cash flow and a higher outlook

For the nine months ended October 31, operating cash flow rose $2 billion to $29.4 billion, while free cash flow fell $2 billion to $6.8 billion on higher capital spending. Walmart held $13.4 billion in cash against $64.3 billion in debt, and repurchased $2.7 billion of stock in the quarter.

Management now expects fiscal 2027 net sales to grow 4.9% to 5.2% in constant currency, up from 4.0% to 5.0%, adjusted operating income to grow 8.0% to 8.6%, up from 7.0% to 8.5%, and adjusted EPS of $2.84 to $2.89, up from $2.80 to $2.87, according to Dow Jones. Capital spending is still expected at about 4% of net sales, and the delayed Flipkart sale should lift the holiday quarter.
